absent: Layout and operations of flavor control and per-CPU queue objects, segmented callback list mechanics, and timer plus deferred-work structures beyond the enqueue and expiry uses observed.
Meaning, defaults and update protocol for sharing controls, contention bounds, lazy thresholds and CPU identifier limits.
Lifecycle of the service thread pointer, creation timing, grace-period engine, and interpretation of urgent request levels.
Purpose and contract of the internal wake sentinel handler and early initialization requirements for callback lists.
Full torture operations structure definition, default values for unobserved members, and registration of the conditional flavor tables.
Complete writer dispatch beyond the initial cases shown in the truncated first part, including remaining synchronization families and pipe-length handling.
Definitions of torture object allocation, pipe counting, stall controls, grace sequence types and writer-state name tables.
Force-quiescent primitive effects, polling cookie formats, and boost inversion check contracts for specific flavors.

findings.text: Enqueue service for tasks flavor callbacks. Accepts a callback node plus handler plus flavor control object. Guarantees node is linked as singleton and associated with handler before becoming visible to grace machinery. Selects a destination per-CPU queue derived from current execution location and configured sharing factor, constrained to possible set. Hands node to segmented list and arranges eventual grace-period wakeup through timer or deferred work.

Interrupt and read-side exclusion around enqueue. Caller context has interrupts saved and disabled while per-CPU queue lock is held, with restore on release. A tasks read-side critical section spans queue selection through enqueue decision, preventing grace progress from bypassing the new callback. Contention fallback from try acquisition to blocking acquisition occurs with interrupts already disabled. Global mode adjustment uses separate global protection associated with cbs_gbl_lock with interrupt save, taken only after per-CPU release.

Queue sharing and contention accounting. Destination derives from shifted local identifier mapped forward to next possible member, with out-of-range treated as programming error. Per-queue retry statistics reset when tick value changes, otherwise increment on contended acquisition. A request to collapse sharing to fully per-CPU is latched only while contention exceeds configured bound and current limit indicates sharing remains; the actual transition happens after per-CPU release under global protection and is announced once.

Wake urgency and lazy deferral policy. Urgency is forced when no service thread exists yet and queue was empty, when handler equals the internal wake sentinel, or when queued count reaches lazy threshold. Otherwise with a live service thread and no pending lazy timer, expiry derived from present tick plus configured lazy interval is programmed when lazy deferral is enabled, else emptiness determines wake need. Urgent marking requests multiple accelerated grace periods. Final wake is deferred to interrupt-context work only when wake is needed and service thread pointer is observed set.

Initialization and deadlock hazards around enqueue. Use before segmented list enablement is diagnosed and repaired by local initialization, since pre-initialization queuing lacks support. Mode collapse is deferred outside per-CPU critical section to avoid lock ordering deadlock. Thread creation and direct wakeup are avoided with disabled interrupts because scheduler protection may be held; creation waits for early init phase and wakeup uses deferred interrupt work.
Lazy expiry helper returning a future tick value based on current tick plus flavor-specific lazy delay. Used to program per-queue timers when immediate wake is not required.

Torture expedited synchronization probe combining classic tasks and normal grace mechanisms through a multi-flavor wait primitive. Exercised as the expedited path for the classic tasks torture binding.

Classic tasks torture binding associates a short textual label and flavor tag with capability flags for interrupt context and slow grace behavior. Read-side group uses tasks-specific entry and exit plus reused pacing. Update-side group uses normal wait, combined expedited wait, direct enqueue, deferred release and barrier. Observability group uses stubbed sequence accessor with diagnostics and grace data collection plus generic init.

Conditional inclusion control for classic tasks binding. One build configuration exposes the binding address with list separator for static table construction; the alternate configuration expands to nothing, omitting the flavor from the built set.

Rude tasks torture binding. Carries distinct flavor tag and hyphenated label with interrupt allowance and bounded flood count. Read-side uses trivial enter and exit plus reused pacing. Update-side provides only normal and expedited waits that map to the same rude wait primitive, with no callback or barrier entry. Observability uses stubbed sequence accessor with rude-specific thread diagnostics and grace data plus generic init.

Conditional inclusion control for rude tasks binding. One build configuration exposes the binding address with list separator for static table construction; the alternate configuration expands to nothing, omitting the flavor from the built set.

Tracing torture read entry mixing two read-side mechanisms. Selection derives from low bits of current tick value, choosing classic suspension on one outcome and tracing suspension otherwise, returning a selector that records which mechanism was taken for matched exit.
Matched exit for mixed tracing read entry. Consumes the selector produced on entry and releases the corresponding classic or tracing critical section, preserving pairing across the randomized choice.
Tracing torture deferred release path forwarding the embedded callback node of a torture object to the tracing enqueue service with the common torture callback handler.

Tracing tasks torture binding. Presents its own flavor tag and hyphenated label with interrupt allowance, slow grace expectation and bounded flood count. Pacing reuses sleepable variant and held-state query checks tracing hold status. Read entry and exit use randomized mixed helpers. Update coverage is fuller than rude variant, offering normal and expedited waits, expedite-current query, direct enqueue, deferred release and barrier. Sequencing uses tracing batch completion with sequence difference helper, plus generic init and tracing-specific diagnostics and data collection.

Conditional inclusion control for tracing tasks binding. One build configuration exposes the binding address with list separator for static table construction; the alternate configuration expands to nothing, omitting the flavor from the built set.

Grace sequence distance helper. Defers to flavor-specific difference operation when the current binding provides one; otherwise falls back to unsigned arithmetic difference between new and old values.

Real-time throttling suspension around boost testing. Saved runtime value named old_rt_runtime uses negative sentinel to mean no suspension active. Disable path acts only for built-in torture and when no suspension is active, capturing current throttle setting before disabling. Enable path acts only for built-in torture when a saved value exists, restoring captured setting and reinstating sentinel.

Boost inversion failure assessment. Elapsed time beyond configured boost duration less half-second tolerance triggers revalidation under ordering to avoid false positives from concurrent grace completion. An optional flavor-specific inversion check can declare technical pass and rate-limit persistence notices to one per interval via atomic update. First failure emits thread priority and grace state plus optional thread diagnostics with completion recheck; every timeout increments a global failure counter.

Boost kthread lifecycle. After optional holdoff sleep honoring stop requests, the thread adopts low real-time priority and cycles through waiting for next interval start with interruptible sleep and stutter handling, then driving grace polls within the interval while launching new polls as prior ones complete and flagging overruns once per interval, then publishing the next interval start exactly once across racing threads, then stuttering before next cycle until a global stop is requested, ending with a stop-absorbing shutdown phase.

Shared boost schedule protection. Interval start associated with boost_starttime is observed with ordered loads and published with ordered stores. Advancement to next interval occurs only under dedicated protection associated with boost_mutex acquired opportunistically in a short sleep retry loop, with double-checked equality ensuring a single publisher increments the global boost count.

Force-quiescent kthread cycle. Each iteration sleeps until a stutter-scaled resume point with stop awareness, then issues a burst of flavor force-quiescent requests spaced by microsecond holds until the configured burst budget is exhausted or stop is requested, then observes global stutter with priority restoration before repeating until global stop, terminating with standard thread shutdown marking.

Enabled update-variant registry. Fixed storage named synctype is sized by the count of writer-state names and holds selected variant codes in fill order, accompanied by separate count named nsynctypes that also serves as insertion cursor during setup and as modulus bound during random selection.

Update-variant enablement policy. Local copies of user selectors default to full enablement when none are requested. Each variant is admitted only when the current binding supplies its required primitives for conditional, expedited, polling, full-state and normal families; admitted variants append a code and emit informational notice, while requested-but-unsupported variants emit alert without admission. Final counts and wait-mode flags are summarized.

Hotplug exclusion around polled cookie capture in synchronous torture updates. A CPU-read hold spans optional cookie acquisition and later validation when randomized polling is active for basic or full-state families, preventing online set changes from invalidating captured grace state across the enclosed waits.

Synchronous update validation contract. Randomized choice enables basic and full-state cookie capture independently. A flavor-indicated double-wait requirement triggers an extra wait before the mandatory wait. Post-wait validation warns when a previously captured cookie is not reported complete, including online set context in diagnostics.

Deferred barrier work handler invoked from workqueue context. Forwards to the current binding barrier operation when present, otherwise performs no action. Used to flush lazy callbacks without blocking the issuer.

Writer kthread main behavior observed in first part. Startup validates expedite control source, aborts with warning when no update variants are enabled, sizes optional poll-state storage from binding active limits, waits for kernel boot completion with elapsed notice, and prepares on-stack lazy work when lazy support is compiled. Steady operation allocates torture objects, publishes them with ordered pointer update and memory separation from retirement accounting, caps pipe-length statistics, then under read protection validates that fresh cookies are not prematurely complete including completed-state rechecks, before dispatching the retired object through a randomly selected enabled variant.

Writer-side grace correctness checks. Holding a read section while capturing a fresh cookie must observe incompleteness; observing completeness triggers a warning with writer-state context. Completed-state captures must conversely observe completeness. Failures indicate grace tracking or read-side pairing defects.
Torture flavor labels are short identifiers: classic tasks uses tasks, rude variant uses tasks-rude, tracing variant uses tasks-tracing.
Numeric protocol values: urgent grace level equals 3; tracing read selection masks tick with 0xff; basic poll gating masks randomness with 0x300 while full-state gating uses 0xc00.
Inactive throttle-save sentinel equals -1, indicating no captured runtime is held.
